policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: The presence or absence of the article before δέησις is invisible in English; ASV 'my supplication to God' renders either. No note is mapped here.
ASV reads 'is for them, that they may be saved' — a bare pronoun. The RP reading τοῦ Ἰσραήλ ἐστιν would have been rendered 'for Israel'; ASV names no nation here.

ASV 'seeking to establish their own' leaves the noun elliptical, with no supplied italic 'righteousness'. The expanded reading ἰδίαν δικαιοσύνην would have given an explicit 'their own righteousness'.

ASV 'Moses writeth that the man that doeth...' attaches ὅτι directly to the verb of writing; the r02 order (ὅτι after τὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ τοῦ νόμου) would have yielded a rendering like 'Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, that...' — so r02 is excluded. Between the base and the WH order the English does not distinguish, since both place ὅτι first.
The article before νόμου is not represented separately in English; ASV 'which is of the law' renders either reading.

ASV gives ποιήσας a single explicit object, 'doeth the righteousness which is of the law', with no resumptive plural. The added αὐτὰ would have produced 'doeth them' alongside the fronted righteousness, as in the older 'doeth those things'.
ASV 'shall live thereby' takes up the one antecedent 'the righteousness' it has just supplied as the object; the plural αὐτοῖς is rendered 'by them' in the tradition ASV departs from here.
The mapped textual_variant note assigns 'confess the word with thy mouth' to 'some ancient authorities', i.e. to the margin; the ASV text 'confess with thy mouth Jesus as Lord' has no τὸ ῥῆμα.
Same mapped textual_variant note: the marginal form is 'that Jesus is Lord', with ὅτι, while the ASV text reads the object-complement 'Jesus as Lord' without it.
Aorist subjunctive and future indicative are alike rendered by ASV 'shall they call on him'; English marks no such contrast and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'shall they believe' renders subjunctive and future indicative alike; the English does not distinguish the readings.
ASV 'shall they hear' renders subjunctive and future indicative alike; the English does not distinguish the readings.
ASV 'shall they preach' renders subjunctive and future indicative alike; the English does not distinguish the readings.
καθὼς and καθάπερ are both rendered 'even as'; ASV 'even as it is written' does not distinguish them.

ASV has the single phrase 'the feet of them that bring glad tidings of good things'; the RP expansion would have added the first Isaiah clause, 'that preach the gospel of peace', which ASV does not have.
The article before ἀγαθά is not separately rendered; ASV 'good things' is compatible with its presence or absence.
ASV reads 'by the word of Christ', naming Χριστοῦ; the RP reading θεοῦ would have given 'the word of God'.
The two readings differ only in the order of Ἰσραὴλ and οὐκ ἔγνω; ASV 'Did Israel not know?' follows English interrogative word order and cannot distinguish them.
ASV 'I was found of them that sought me not' renders the dative alone; the preposition ἐν leaves no separate trace in the English.
ASV 'I became manifest unto them that asked not of me' renders the dative alone; an added ἐν would leave no distinct mark in the English.
